T lymphocytes], which may be what destroys the beta-cells in diabetes); and (4) auto-
antibodies to the tyrosine phosphatases IA-2 and IA-2β.4 Frequently, after diagnosis 
and the correction of hyperglycemia, metabolic acidosis, and ketoacidosis, endogenous 
insulin secretion recovers. During this “honeymoon phase”, exogenous insulin 
requirements decrease dramatically. However, the need for exogenous insulin is 
­inevitable, and within 8–10 years after clinical onset, beta-cell loss is complete and 
insulin deficiency is absolute.3–5
